summary.headline: Repco Home Finance Q2 FY27: September-quarter disbursement of Rs.1,205 Cr; gross NPA cut to 2.4% and FY27 PAT guided at Rs.480-490 Cr.
summary.overview: Management reported Q2 FY27 disbursements of about Rs.1,205 Cr, up from Rs.1,069 Cr in the prior-year period, and said it had crossed Rs.1,000 Cr per quarter in every quarter since September 2025 except June 2026. Gross NPA fell to Rs.396-398 Cr (2.4%) from Rs.426-427 Cr at end-June, and stage 2 assets fell year-on-year to Rs.1,154 Cr. Net profit was about Rs.116 Cr versus Rs.114 Cr in Q1 and about Rs.106 Cr a year earlier. Management guided to higher disbursements in Q3 and Q4, a sub-2% gross NPA by year-end, and a spread drifting down to about 3.2-3.3% as funding costs rise and retention concessions are passed on.

segments.name: Housing loans
segments.commentary: About 71% of AUM; yield about 11.07%. Salaried customers yield about 11.25% and non-salaried about 12.07% (as stated).

segments.name: Non-housing loans
segments.commentary: About 29% of AUM; yield about 13.32%. Builder loans: nil exposure per management.

segments.name: Geography
segments.commentary: About 57% of book from Tamil Nadu, remainder non-TN; management expects non-TN share to rise. Branch network 242 including satellite centres, with 13-14 new branches planned this year, mostly non-TN.

guidance_outlook: Q3 FY27 disbursement guidance Rs.1,300-1,350 Cr; Q4 FY27 Rs.1,650-1,700 Cr; total for the current half about Rs.3,000-3,050 Cr.
Gross NPA to be brought below 2% by year-end (from 2.4%).
FY27 profit expected at about Rs.480-490 Cr; H1 FY27 profit about Rs.230 Cr.
Credit cost: provision charge of about Rs.5-6 Cr per quarter in Q3 and Q4, with no further reversals taken.
Cost of funds expected to rise by at least 10-15 bps; increase to be passed on to borrowers with about one-quarter lag.
Spread to settle at about 3.2-3.3% in the near term (ALCO due at month-end to decide pass-through).
Cost-to-income ratio expected to stay stable at current level.
Dividend payout ratio not yet decided; final dividend to be set with year-end results.
capex_capacity: Branch network 242 including satellite centres; plan to open 12-14 more branches this year, majority outside Tamil Nadu.
Around 50 branches opened over the last two to three years.
Digitalisation in two phases: core and mobile applications live; integration with CERSAI and CIBIL to cut turnaround time; mobile app for sourcing executives in progress.
Verticalisation: separate verticals for sales, recovery, collections, operations, credit and SARFAESI.
demand_pricing: Disbursement growth driven by DST (direct sales team) recruitment, a connector model, expanded DSA channel and a revised incentive structure with a special incentive for sourcing channels.
June 2026 disbursement of about Rs.843 Cr was below the Rs.1,000 Cr target, attributed to staff transfers and promotions; incentives for Q1 deferred and paid with September.
Retention concessions given to long-standing good-CIBIL customers to arrest balance-transfer outflow (BT Out); management said returns and quality do not come together.
Minimum lending rate about 9.9%, depending on borrower risk profile. Average ticket size about Rs.23-25 lakh incremental, overall book about Rs.14 lakh.
Book split: non-salaried 53.6%, salaried 46.4%. No builder-loan exposure.

qa_highlights.question: Guidance for Q3 and Q4 disbursement, and October trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Q3 guided at Rs.1,300-1,350 Cr and Q4 at Rs.1,650-1,700 Cr; management said October and month-to-date disbursement were in line and it was confident of the Q3 number.

qa_highlights.question: Credit cost and FY27 PAT outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Provision charge of Rs.5-6 Cr per quarter expected in Q3 and Q4; FY27 profit guided at about Rs.480-490 Cr versus H1 about Rs.230 Cr.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q3 disbursement break its historical pattern of falling below Q2, and what drives opex?
qa_highlights.answer: Raja said independent sales and credit channels now remove overlap, allowing focus on business. Opex rose on incentive payouts for deferred Q1 incentives, actuarial true-up of gratuity and leave encashment, recruitment of branch sales managers and recovery staff, 5-10% performance-linked increments, and higher DSA payouts.

qa_highlights.question: Sensitivity of borrowing costs to repo hikes and asset-side repricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Entire liability book floating except a special NHB scheme; entire asset book floating and reprices every three months. Cost of funds expected to rise 10-15 bps, passed on with about one-quarter lag; spread to fall to about 3.25-3.3%.

qa_highlights.question: Are there any housing-loan stress signals in South India, particularly Karnataka?
qa_highlights.answer: No stress seen in the South; Karnataka disbursement was below normal in Q1 and improved in Q2. Cheque return ratios stable.

qa_highlights.question: Why did spreads widen about 30 bps and yields rise to around 12%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a half-year yield of 11.83% and cost of funds of 8.35%, a spread of 3.47%. Some lenders have raised rates but not yet passed on; spread expected to stabilise around 3.2-3.25% in one to two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Exposure to drought-affected areas and asset-quality risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it assessed drought-hit areas, but the book is mainly urban and metro periphery, Tier-1 and Tier-2, with no stress observed.

risks_watch: Spread compression to about 3.2-3.3% as cost of funds rises 10-15 bps and retention concessions are given; ALCO outcome at end-October/November is key.
Gross NPA must fall from 2.4% to below 2% by year-end; provision charges of Rs.5-6 Cr per quarter in H2 with no further reversals.
Execution on disbursement ramp (Q3 Rs.1,300-1,350 Cr, Q4 Rs.1,650-1,700 Cr) depends on DST/DSA productivity; June 2026 shortfall shows sensitivity to staff transfers.
Opex and cost-to-income: salary costs rose on incentives and recruitment; management says ratio will stay stable.
Funding: rating upgrade expected once NPA is below 2%; NHB refinance of Rs.600 Cr sanctioned, Rs.231 Cr drawn so far; further NHB schemes possible.
Dividend payout policy not defined; management gave no payout ratio.
Promoter-linked deputation change at Repco Bank (Vaidyanathan withdrawn, Kannan posted); management called it administrative and said there is no promoter interference.
summary.management_tone: Confident and specific on disbursement and asset-quality targets, with numbers given for Q3, Q4 and the full year. More guarded on margins, where management openly said the spread will fall. Vague on dividend payout ratio, saying no number has been set.

adds.what: 13-14 new branches planned this year, mostly outside Tamil Nadu (on a 242-branch network)

growth.why: Q3 and Q4 disbursement guidance of Rs1,300-1,350 Cr and Rs1,650-1,700 Cr plus FY27 PAT of Rs480-490 Cr, backed by DST recruitment, DSA expansion and 13-14 new branches; no order-book-style hard numbers on capacity beyond the branch plan.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Spread guided to fall to about 3.2-3.3% from about 3.4-3.47% as cost of funds rises 10-15 bps and retention concessions are passed on, so margin expansion is not expected.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Management plans 12-14 new branches this year (on a 242-branch network, about 5.6%), mostly outside Tamil Nadu, with DST recruitment ramping alongside.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Disbursement guided to Rs.1,300-1,350 Cr in Q3 and Rs.1,650-1,700 Cr in Q4 versus Rs.1,205 Cr in Q2, with October reported in line; AUM up about 9% YoY to Rs.16,425 Cr.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 PAT guided at Rs.480-490 Cr against H1 of about Rs.230 Cr implies a steep H2 ramp, with Rs.5-6 Cr quarterly provisions and spread compression ahead, leaving little room to raise guidance.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Spread already cut to 3.2-3.3% and the ALCO pass-through decision is pending, while the Q3-Q4 disbursement ramp depends on DST/DSA productivity, which fell short in June 2026 (Rs.843 Cr vs Rs.1,000 Cr target).

rows.label: Gross NPA below 2% by year-end
rows.why: Gross NPA fell from Rs.475 Cr (Sept 2025) to Rs.396 Cr (2.4%), and management set an internal target below 2% by year-end with provisioning of Rs.5-6 Cr per quarter.

rows.label: Rating upgrade once NPA below 2%
rows.why: Management expects a rating upgrade once gross NPA is below 2%, with NHB refinance of Rs.600 Cr sanctioned and Rs.231 Cr drawn so far, which would lower funding costs.

rows.label: Pass-through of higher cost of funds
rows.why: Cost of funds expected to rise 10-15 bps with about one-quarter lag, and the ALCO decision at month-end sets the pass-through to borrowers.

tone.note: Management was confident on disbursement ramp (Q3 Rs.1,300-1,350 Cr, Q4 Rs.1,650-1,700 Cr) and sub-2% gross NPA by year-end, but openly guided spread lower and gave no dividend payout ratio; analysts probed spread compression, credit cost and opex.
